learn.b: PHP is a language that runs on a web server and builds web pages before they are sent to the browser. PHP code lives in files ending in .php and sits between the tags <?php and ?>.
echo prints text into the page. Every PHP statement must end with a semicolon. Text goes in quotes, either single or double.
A .php file can contain normal HTML with PHP blocks inside it. Only the output of the PHP part reaches the browser, never the PHP code itself.
Comments are ignored by PHP. Use // or # for one line and /* ... */ for many lines. print also outputs text, but echo is the usual choice.

learn.b: A variable name starts with a dollar sign. You create one by assigning a value with =. There are no type keywords. Names are case sensitive.
PHP has string, int, float, bool and array, plus null for no value. The type comes from the value, and PHP changes types automatically when needed.
var_dump shows both the type and the value. gettype gives the type name. You can cast with (int), (string) and so on.
A constant never changes. Create one with define or const, and use it without a dollar sign. By convention names are capitals.

learn.b: Double quotes read variables inside them, and single quotes do not. Escapes like \n work only in double quotes. Join strings with a dot.
strlen gives the length. strpos finds where text starts, counting from 0, and gives false if not found. str_contains tests for text in PHP 8 and later.
strtoupper and strtolower change case. str_replace swaps text. substr cuts a piece. trim removes spaces at the ends. ucfirst capitalizes the first letter.
explode splits a string into an array using a separator. implode joins an array into a string. Use heredoc or sprintf for longer text and formatting.

learn.b: Math operators are + - * / % and ** for power. Assignment shortcuts include +=, -= and .= for strings. ++ adds one. Comparison uses ==, ===, != and <, >.
== compares values after converting types, so 5 == "5" is true. === also compares the type, so 5 === "5" is false. Prefer === to avoid surprises.
if runs code when a condition is true. Combine conditions with && (and), || (or) and !. Use elseif (one word) for extra branches.
match returns a value and uses strict comparison (PHP 8). The null coalescing operator ?? gives a default when a value is missing or null. A switch statement is the older alternative.

qs.q: Which comparison also checks the type?

qs.why: elseif is the PHP keyword, one word.

<?php
$age = 15;
if ($age >= 18) {
    echo "adult";
} elseif ($age >= 13) {
    echo "teen";
} else {
    echo "kid";
}
?>
qs.why: 15 is not 18 or more but is 13 or more.

qs.q: In PHP, 5 === "5" is true.
qs.why: The types differ, so strict comparison fails.

learn.b: while repeats as long as its condition is true. Change something inside the loop, or it never ends.
for puts the start, the test and the step in one line, separated by semicolons.
foreach goes through every item of an array. Add key => value to get keys too. It is the loop you will use most in PHP.
break stops the loop. continue jumps to the next round. do-while runs the body once before testing.

learn.b: An array holds many values. Create it with square brackets. Positions are numbered from 0. Use count to get the size and [] to add at the end.
An associative array uses names as keys instead of numbers. Write key => value pairs.
foreach with $key => $value goes through pairs. Use isset to test if a key exists and unset to remove one.
array_push adds at the end, array_pop removes the last, in_array checks for a value, array_keys lists keys, sort orders values, and array_merge joins arrays. print_r displays an array.

learn.b: Use the function keyword, a name, parameters and a body. return sends back a value. Call it by name with parentheses.
You can give parameters and results types, and defaults with =. Add declare(strict_types=1) at the top to make type checks strict.
Variables made inside a function are local and not visible outside. Variables outside are not visible inside unless you pass them as arguments. The global keyword exists but is best avoided.
fn is short for small functions, like fn($x) => $x * 2. They are handy with array_map and array_filter. PHP also has hundreds of built-in functions, such as strlen and count.

learn.b: A form sends data to a PHP file. The action says where to send it, and method says how: get puts data in the URL and post sends it in the request body. Each input has a name.
These are special arrays that hold the data. The input's name is the key. Use $_GET for links and searches, and $_POST for forms that change things or send private data.
A visitor may leave a field out, so check it first. isset tests if a key exists, empty tests for blank values, and ?? gives a default. $_SERVER["REQUEST_METHOD"] tells you if the form was sent.
Anything from a form can be changed by a visitor. Validate it, for example with filter_var, and clean it before output. Use htmlspecialchars when printing user text to stop XSS attacks.

learn.b: A class is a blueprint, and an object is one thing made from it with new. Properties hold data and methods are functions in the class. Use -> to reach them, and $this inside the class.
The method __construct runs when an object is created. PHP 8 lets you declare properties right in its parameters. Visibility keywords are public, protected and private.
A class can extend another and gets its properties and methods. parent:: reaches the parent's version. static members belong to the class and are used with ::.
An interface lists methods a class must have. A class says implements. Together with abstract classes and traits they keep big programs organized.

learn.b: PDO is PHP's way to talk to many databases such as MySQL or SQLite with the same code. You create a connection with a DSN, a username and a password, and tell it to throw exceptions on errors.

Never put user input directly into SQL, because that allows SQL injection. Use a prepared statement with placeholders, then pass the values to execute. The database treats them as data, never as code.
fetch returns one row and fetchAll returns all rows as arrays. For inserts, call execute with the values. Named placeholders such as :name make longer queries easier to read.
Escape user text with htmlspecialchars before printing it in HTML to stop XSS. Store passwords with password_hash and check them with password_verify, never as plain text.

qs.q: What protects SQL queries from injection?
qs.why: Placeholders keep data separate from SQL code.
